description:
The error catalogue marks bitstring-segment and bitstring-use as planned (kind :planned in lib/defk/errors.ex) but no ticket tracked them; found while writing the scope page (defk-djy.5), which lists every planned item with its ticket.

Today an append to a bitstring accumulator takes big-endian integer segments only (v::size(n), v::k, v, optionally signed), and a bitstring is output only: it starts from <<>>, is appended to, measured with bit_size/1 and returned; a kernel cannot read one, start one from an input binary, and Elixir cannot pass one to an entry kernel. The catalogue's own wording is 'not supported until a workload needs them'.

Done when a target workload needs one of these (name it here), the chosen segment types or reads have an Elixir-mode meaning and agreement properties, and the two codes' entries (or their kind) are updated; or the items are moved to :subset with the reason recorded.
title: Bitstring accumulator: little-endian, float and binary segments, and reading a bitstring (when a workload needs them)
